title: Higher-Order Functions
subtitle: Pass a function, return a function, and count the calls
description: Turn three near-identical sums into one function that takes its rule as an argument, then build fixed-point search, average damping and Newton's method from functions that take and return functions.
estimateNote: Author estimate, not measured on learners: lesson 20–25 minutes, lab 45–70 minutes. The book's own text is a reference and is not counted.
sourceAttribution: Follows section 1.3 of Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs by Harold Abelson and Gerald Jay Sussman with Julie Sussman (MIT Press, 2nd ed. 1996; CC BY-SA 4.0), with its examples and exercises 1.32, 1.42 and 1.43 rewritten in Python. Prose and lab are original. Independent course; not endorsed by MIT or UC Berkeley.
